item.title: French policeman jailed for eight years on appeal over 2020 killing of motorist
item.description: Olivio Gomes’s family called the verdict historic as figures show ethnic minorities are four times more likely to be stopped by police in France.

item.title: Strasbourg, Birmingham and Baden-Baden: Europe’s top 10 most accessible Christmas markets
item.description: This new study looked at factors like the distance to step-free public transport and the share of uneven ground in the surrounding area to create the ranking.

item.title: 'Grand Theft Auto VI' released after 13-year wait, selling over 17 million copies
item.description: The series lets players live out gangster fantasies, smash up cars and fight whoever they choose in a fictionalised US city populated by lowlifes, sex workers and thugs.

item.title: What advice has Pierce Brosnan given new James Bond actor Robert Pattinson?
item.description: Brosnan was the fifth actor to portray the iconic spy, starting with 'GoldenEye' in 1995.

item.title: Record breaker: Vincent van Gogh painting sells for €173 m to settle row over its Nazi past
item.description: Vincent van Gogh's painting "Chestnut Trees in Bloom", has fetched a record €173 million at Sotheby's in New York, the most expensive sale for a work by the Dutch artist. It is the fourth most expensive artwork ever sold at auction.

item.title: The world’s best airlines have just been announced for 2027 – with no European carriers in the top 10
item.description: The inaugural list from TIME crowned the UAE flag carrier Emirates as the best overall, despite travel disruption in the Middle East over the past nine months.

item.title: China: Trump calls Putin his "friend" as leaders meet amid in Shenzhen
item.description: Donald Trump greeted Vladimir Putin as his friend during a meeting in Shenzhen. Their 40-minute encounter came ahead of trilateral talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping.

item.title: Meet the seven Anthropic founders whose fortunes could grow by billions
item.description: From former OpenAI researchers to a British technology journalist, the people behind the Claude chatbot could each see their fortunes soar even further into the billions when the company goes public.

item.title: Ukraine: Four killed and at least 13 injured in Russian strike on Odesa
item.description: Russian strikes on the historic centre of Odesa, Ukraine, killed four people and injured at least 13 others on Wednesday 18 November 2026, according to the city’s military administration.

item.title: Giving a solo founder the horsepower of a multinational — affordably
item.description: European small businesses have ambition and creativity, but lack time and budgets. As Kuo Zhang of Alibaba.com writes in an op-ed for Euronews, affordable, ready-to-use AI and global supply chain tools give even solo founders the capabilities of global companies, freeing them to focus on growth.

item.title: If Europe is not around the table, is it on the menu?
item.description: Good morning. Angela Skujins penning your Thursday newsletter. On today’s docket: Friends of Ukraine meet in the German capital while a potentially consequential trilateral gets underway in China.

item.title: Europe Today: Xi, Trump and Putin together in a historic trilateral meeting
item.description: The heads of state of China, Russia and the US are expected to discuss denuclearization and the Iran war, but not Ukraine. We speak with Kremlin critic Bill Browder. The Coalition of the Willing will meet in Berlin, we talk about it with Ignacy Niemczycki, Poland Deputy Foreign Minister.

item.title: Geopolitics and genuine bonds: Negotiators on what it's like behind the scenes as COP tensions build
item.description: 'We're constantly surrounded by people and we sleep very little, five hours a night at most.'

item.title: Europe wants households ready for crises. But what if you can't prepare?
item.description: New EU guidelines urge citizens to manage the first 72 hours of an emergency independently. Commissioner Hadja Lahbib said it “has become an internationally recognised benchmark for household emergency preparedness.” Yet a University of Latvia survey found that only 8% feel prepared.

item.title: North Korea expanding original uranium enrichment facility, UN nuclear watchdog says
item.description: The IAEA has not had access to Yongbyon or other locations in North Korea since the country kicked out the agency’s inspectors in 2009.

item.title: Chronically online? ‘Problematic internet use’ is a growing global health concern, experts warn
item.description: Experts called for stricter regulation of digital platforms, warning that features designed to keep users online can fuel harmful internet use.

item.title: Europe must make the EU–UK Security and Defence Partnership work
item.description: 'Europe’s security environment will not wait for perfect alignment. Our leaders should seize the opportunities within reach. Our industry needs them to do so,' write Micael Johansson and David Lockwood, senior representatives of the European aerospace, security and defence industries, in an op-ed.

item.title: Ho ho homework: London's Santa School prepares Father Christmas performers for the festive season
item.description: Professional Santas are heading back to school in South London to prepare for the Christmas season.Training includes everything from sign language and the latest toy trends to handling difficult questions from children.

item.title: Historic trilateral summit between leaders of the US, China and Russia begins
item.description: The three-president meeting at the Kylin Villa, which analysts expect to be heavier in symbolism than concrete breakthroughs, comes with Russia's offensive in Ukraine approaching the five-year mark. Trump met Putin earlier greeting him with "who is he ? He's my friend !"

item.title: France: Hundreds raise a glass to Beaujolais Nouveau in Lyon
item.description: Lyon welcomed the arrival of Beaujolais Nouveau with a lively nighttime parade of wine barrels, flaming torches and brass music. Hundreds gathered to celebrate the first tastings of this year's wine.

item.title: Rare stonefly found beside vanishing glacier on Chile's Navarino Island
item.description: An international team of scientists, including researchers from the University of Barcelona, has discovered a rare insect beside the remains of a glacier in Chilean Patagonia.

item.title: The dark side of AI: US data centres emit more carbon than all of Denmark
item.description: The Harvard study has revealed that pledges alone might not be enough, even as COP31 negotiators push for cleaner energy use in data centres.

item.title: EU plans a new €45bn loan to Ukraine. How much will it cost? And will it be repaid?
item.description: Euronews breaks down the European Commission's new proposal to issue a €45 billion support loan to Ukraine. Here's what you need to know.

item.title: Festive train trips: Europe’s most magical Christmas and winter rail journeys
item.description: Get the festive season on the right track with these unique European winter and Christmas rail journeys, offering luxury, adventure and slow travel.

item.title: China: Xi, Trump and Putin gather ahead of trilateral summit
item.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping, US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin appeared together in Shenzhen, on Thursday 19 November 2026, posing for a group photograph alongside other world leaders ahead of a closely watched trilateral summit.

item.title: Zelenskyy says he expects debrief from US envoys on Trump’s talks with Xi and Putin
item.description: The US envoys told Kyiv they would give a debrief on the talks being held by Trump in China during meetings in Berlin on Thursday, Zelenskyy said.

item.title: Anthropic's record IPO lands as Nvidia suffers its worst run since 2008
item.description: Anthropic priced its record IPO at $83 a share ahead of Thursday's debut, as Nvidia heads for a seventh weekly loss and Washington tightens AI chip exports.

item.title: Hegseth in Colombia to deepen anti-drug ties after surprise Venezuela stopover
item.description: Colombian Defense Minister Jorge Eduardo Mora had told his country's parliament that the Pentagon chief would hand over a C-130 Hercules military aircraft during the visit.

item.title: GTA VI launch sparks celebrations in Miami and Dublin
item.description: After 13 years of anticipation, Grand Theft Auto VI has finally arrived. Fans celebrated at a launch party in Dublin, while Miami Heat supporters rushed to buy limited-edition Vice City merchandise.

item.title: Alleged Russian agent arrested for spying on Silicon Valley tech firm
item.description: The company was not named in the indictment but was described as a large, publicly traded technology and defence firm with offices across the US, including in Palo Alto, California.

item.title: Bukele confirms airstrike on Haitian gang leader Jeff's luxury mansion
item.description: The Salvadoran president welcomes the destruction of the home of Jeff Larose, one of Haiti's main crime leaders. It is not clear whether Jeff was in the building during the bombing.

item.title: Data watchdog probes massive Deutsche Bank leak of 15M files
item.description: A German state data regulator has opened an investigation on Wednesday into Deutsche Bank following a massive data leak. The authority is investigating possible data protection violations.

item.title: US Defense Secretary announces military cooperation in surprise Caracas visit
item.description: The US Defense Secretary met Delcy Rodríguez in Caracas ahead of a planned visit to Colombia, where he is due to discuss bilateral security cooperation.

item.title: Europe Tonight: former Estonian President Toomas Hendrik Ilves speaks on the future of the global order
item.description: Watch our presenter Mared Gwyn Jones speak live with former Estonian President Toomas Hendrik Ilves to discuss what the summit could mean for Europe and the future of the global order.

item.title: Germany’s Digitalisation Minister Wildberger discusses Europe's AI race with the US and China
item.description: Euronews correspondent Luca Bertuzzi spoke to Germany’s Digitalisation Minister, Karsten Wildberger, about whether Europe can catch up with the US and China in the AI race.

item.title: Are migrant return hubs in Rwanda an effective solution or a dangerous precedent?
item.description: In this edition of our debate show, MEPs Lena Düpont (EPP) and Robert Biedroń (S&D) go face-to-face over the EU's migration policy.

item.title: Faster electrification is essential for Europe to escape fossil fuel shocks, Jørgensen warns
item.description: Energy Commissioner Dan Jørgensen said the latest EU agreement to accelerate permitting procedures is a step forward for clean power and infrastructure to revamp the bloc's obsolete power grid and boost electrification — even if financing the power grid remains yet another obstacle.

item.title: Hakeem Jeffries moves closer to becoming first Black US House speaker
item.description: The New York Democrat secured 251 votes in favour and 11 against, but faces pressure from progressive lawmakers demanding commitments on healthcare, immigration and other key issues.

item.title: Euronews Verify: Can the EU close Russia's sanctions loopholes?
item.description: Another batch of EU sanctions targeting Russian banks, oil refineries and Russia's "shadow fleet" is expected later this month. But are sanctions actually effective against Moscow?

item.title: Former Macron ally Philippe unveils conservative agenda as French centre and right loses ground
item.description: Socialist, centrist and conservative candidates have been struggling to gain ground ahead of France's presidential elections, amid a race dominated by the hard left and far-right.

item.title: French broadcaster faces backlash after revealing feminist guest's marriage live on air
item.description: An activist criticised a French public broadcaster after a presenter revealed her marriage to a senior TV executive, sparking controversy over transparency rules and political reactions.

item.title: No heating or AC needed: Inside the French apartment block retaining heat from cooking and sunlight
item.description: The apartment building is designed to maintain an interior temperature between 20°C and 26°C without heating or air conditioning.

item.title: Europe Tonight: EU proposes €45bn Ukraine loan as Trump, Xi and Putin meet
item.description: Ursula von der Leyen unveils a new joint-debt package for Kyiv, an unprecedented US-China-Russia trilateral summit unfolds at APEC, industry figures warn Europe cannot sleep through the AI revolution.

item.title: Designing Qatar’s new creative economy, from innovation hubs to incubation spaces
item.description: Creativity is becoming part of Qatar’s economic vision. Beyond galleries and exhibition spaces, Qatar is investing in infrastructures designed to nurture creatives so that their concepts can turn into creation.

item.title: EPP ready to suspend Vučić’s SNS party in December
item.description: The party leadership will submit the proposal to the political assembly, where it is expected to secure approval. SNS could make a comeback, provided it meets certain conditions.

item.title: Waymo pulls driverless taxis off US highways after California ban
item.description: Regulators called the robotaxis an "imminent hazard" after one tried to overtake police cars and three others drove into a live roadworks zone, just as the company prepares to expand into Europe.

item.title: Storms Bruna and Charles bring record rain and winds to Portugal and Madeira
item.description: The two storms combined meant that several records for maximum wind gusts and rainfall were broken in the first 12 days of November, according to the Portuguese Institute for the Sea and the Atmosphere (IPMA).

item.title: Israeli military launches new operation on central Gaza despite ceasefire
item.description: The military says it is targeting Hamas infrastructure near two refugee camps, while Hamas has accused Israel of violating the truce in place since October 2025.
